rules_text:
Rules summary How to play 1 Construct your hanging garden (mandatory) a) Select a Garden card b) Place your Garden card c) Resolve your Garden card 2 Reveal a new Garden card (mandatory) 3 Buy a single Enhancement tile (optional) 4 Complete a single Royal Objective (optional) End of round The round ends when all players have placed all their Gardeners. Take back all your Gardeners and begin the next round. If you have played 4 rounds, you have all finished constructing your hanging gardens. Proceed to scoring. Scoring Scoring Score your victory points as follows: • Irrigation: Count the number of irrigated Garden cards in the places specified on your Irrigation card. Score the corresponding number of victory points. • Blooms: Only your largest connected group in each flower color (red, yellow and blue) scores. Gain 1 point per flower in those groups. • Trees: Score the number of points shown for your groups of connected trees of the same species. • Animals: Score the number of points for the level on which your animal is placed. Lions: like to lounge on level 1 Monkeys: like to play on level 2 Peacocks: like the calm on level 3 • Visitors: Score the points shown if the features your visitor wants to see are in your garden. • Royal Objectives: Score the same number of points as Royal Objectives you have completed. The winner is the player with the most victory points. If there is a tie, the winner is the player with the most tools and gold coins. If there is still a tie, the tied players both win.

[Rating: 3/10] A tile drafting game where players place a worker, gaining a tile, and placing it onto their tableau. Each tile has different scoring mechanics. Once a player completes their 5/4/3 tiles per level, points are scored and the most points win.

[Rating: 4/10] Nice art, but does almost nothing to set itself apart from the vast array of abstract tile laying puzzle games that exist nowadays. It sits in a weird spot of being slightly more complex than many of them where I wouldn't necessarily recommend it for very new players, but it also doesn't really have that much going on either. Strange design.

[Rating: 5/10] What makes people 'design' games without any new idea?  I suppose they enjoy the process and it pleases their vanity.
